Arrangement.description: Where each part of one job is, in the graph's order of parts.

Cost.description: A part kind's time on a device, per step, at the batch the device's memory allows.

band.description:
How far a measurement may be from the prediction, relative: taken from past differences
between the two.

estimate.description:
Not measured on this device: estimated from the part's shapes, and so to be probed, not
trusted.

DeviceId.description: A device: its member, and its index on that member.

Dtype.description: What an edge carries: a tensor's element type, or opaque bytes (an encoded image, a record).

Format.description: A file format a pool reads, at the version it reads.

Held.description: A job a pool holds, as the pool's description shows it.

arrangement.description: Where its parts are. The job's name is the arrangement's.

waited_seconds.description: Seconds it has waited since it arrived or last lost its place: 0 while it is placed.

Member.description: A machine in the pool, running `mag-mar`: one lease of the host's.

give_back_seconds.description: Seconds within which the member gives a device back when the host takes it back.

name.description:
A DNS name in lower case, as [`is_member_name`] takes it: the member's certificate
carries it so.

trust.description: How far the host trusts it. Nothing kept at a higher level is placed on its devices.

Offer.description: What a device gives the pool now.

costs.description: Its time per step for each part kind it has run or estimated.

memory_bytes.description: The memory it can give: what is free of anything else holding it.

tolerances.description: The tolerance classes its measured bounds meet.

oneOf.description: A replicable part's copies, one on each device, each pulling items from one queue.

Tolerance.description:
The numerics a part accepts. A device takes the part only if its measured bounds for the
part's operations meet it.

Trust.description:
How far a machine is trusted, and how far data must be kept, in order: `outside < site <
owner`. A member is trusted at a level; an input or a blob is kept at a level, and is placed
only on a member trusted at least as far.

The host gives each member its level, and mag judges no one: what a level means is the
host's. As a rule of thumb, `owner` is the owner's own machines, `site` a machine inside the
owner's site that is not the owner's, and `outside` anything else, a rented machine among
them.

oneOf.description: Trusted with what anyone may hold.
Inside the owner's site, but not the owner's.

description:
The pool as an author sees it, as one virtual device: its members and what each device
offers, where each job it holds is and how long each waiting one has waited, and the file
formats it reads. An author reads it before writing a graph.

at.description: The pool's time, in seconds: the latest it has been told of.

jobs.description: The jobs it holds, in the order they arrived.

members.description:
Its members, each with the lowest trust and the shortest time to give a device back it was
reported with.

offers.description:
What each device offers, with the costs measured or estimated on it, in the order of the
devices' ids.

title: mag-pool, version 2
